financing.summary: Bloomfield Homes, L.P. publishes no financial statements, no debt and no lot count: it is a consolidated subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Forestry (Tokyo: 1911), which bought 50% in June 2013 and went to 65% in May 2017 through Sumitomo Forestry America, with the founders' companies keeping the rest. Its capital therefore comes from the parent group and from whatever bank lines it holds privately; no land banker, lot-option financier or outside capital partner is named for Bloomfield in any source read, and it describes itself as a major land purchaser and developer. The parent reports lots only for its five pre-Tri Pointe US builders together: 73,971 lots at September 30, 2026, of which 50,471 are owned and 23,500 (32%) are under purchase contract, and it has told investors it wants its US builders to buy more land through option contracts to cut the financial burden. That push now has a balance-sheet reason behind it: after the $4.0B Tri Pointe purchase the parent's interest-bearing debt rose to JPY 1,659.7 billion, its equity ratio fell to 29.2%, net debt to equity is about 1.4 times, JPY 260 billion of acquisition funding still needs permanent financing before the SMBC bridge loan falls due on May 10, 2027, and management says a rating downgrade is possible. For a land banker the opening is a majority-owned, owner-developer builder in one market (Dallas-Fort Worth) whose parent wants its US land off the balance sheet, and whose sister companies already use the product (Tri Pointe has land banking arrangements; multifamily affiliate JPI signed with Millrose in 2026).
financing.land_strategy: Owns and develops most of its own land. In its own words Bloomfield has become 'a major land purchaser and developer' that designs its neighbourhoods with local governments; Sumitomo Forestry described its business in 2013 as home building and lot development. It also builds in master plans developed by others (Union Park by Hillwood is one confirmed case) and in communities carrying public improvement district or municipal management district assessments. No owned versus optioned target is published for Bloomfield; the parent's stated direction for all of its US builders is to 'promote land acquisition through option contracts' and lighten the balance sheet (August 2026 strategy briefing).

lots.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry Q3 FY12/2026 Financial Factbook (2026-11-05), U.S. single-family homes pages
lots.note: Bloomfield's own lot count is not publicly disclosed, so the fields are left empty. Group figures that include Bloomfield (Sumitomo Forestry's five US builders excluding Tri Pointe: Bloomfield, DRB Group incl. Brightland, Edge, MainVue, Southern Impression) at September 30, 2026: 73,971 lots in total, 50,471 purchased (owned) and 23,500 under purchase contract, so 31.8% under contract (our division); down 9.5% in a year, with lots under contract down 23.7%. At December 31, 2025 the same five held 79,565 lots (50,894 owned, 28,671 under contract). Against the five builders' 10,262 homes sold in FY2025 that is about 7.2 years of supply (our calculation). Including Tri Pointe the group held 106,415 lots (67,154 owned, 39,261 under option or contract). The parent's South Central (Texas) region, where Bloomfield is one of three group builders, sold 3,517 homes in FY2025; in January to September 2026 it sold 2,938 including Tri Pointe and 2,267 for the pre-Tri Pointe builders (down 14.8% year on year). Only historical Bloomfield figure found: 3,500 lots secured in Dallas-Fort Worth at the June 2013 investment (https://sfc.jp/english/pdf/20130701.pdf).

land_banking.counterparty: Sumitomo Forestry America, Inc. (subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd.)
land_banking.description: Majority owner and the visible source of capital. Sumitomo Forestry bought 50% of Bloomfield in June 2013 and a further 15% for $36.5M in May 2017, making Bloomfield a consolidated subsidiary at 65%. Tri Pointe's February 2026 merger communications describe Sumitomo Forestry's US builders, Bloomfield among them, as locally led brands that share the group's scale, capital support and long-term investment; in 2026 the parent is steering them toward option contracts for land. Terms of any parent loans, guarantees or capital contributions to Bloomfield are not published.
land_banking.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice regarding acquisition of additional equity interest in Bloomfield Homes, L.P. which will become a subsidiary (2017-04-28)
land_banking.note: Not a land-banking arrangement: listed because the parent is who funds Bloomfield. The $36.5M is the 2017 price for the extra 15%, not a facility size. The 2026 Texas franchise-tax record shows four Sumitomo Forestry designees (Addison, TX office address) on the board of the general partner, Bloomfield Properties, Inc., beside the two founders and Deborah Dykstra (https://comptroller.texas.gov/data-search/franchise-tax/32015762365). 'Capital support' wording is from Tri Pointe's February 13, 2026 merger communications (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000119312526051652/d81161ddefa14a.htm); option-contract direction from the August 10, 2026 strategy briefing (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_2q_strategy_02_en.pdf).

land_banking.description: Bloomfield is one of two builders listed in Union Park, a master plan developed by Hillwood; the other is its new sister company Tri Pointe Homes. This shows Bloomfield also takes lots in third-party master plans rather than only developing its own. Lot counts, prices and takedown terms are not public.
land_banking.source_title: Union Park by Hillwood: Builders page (retrieved 2026-11-19, undated)
land_banking.note: The developer's page names the builders but says nothing about contract structure, so whether these are option takedowns or bulk purchases is unknown. Bloomfield's own Union Park pages confirm it sells there and show the Highway 380 Municipal Management District No. 1 on the lots (https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/little-elm/union-park-classic-55/). Other third-party master plans on Bloomfield's community list were not checked against developer sites. Verification 2026-11-19: upgraded from Reported to Verified; both the developer's own builders page (lists Bloomfield Homes and Tri Pointe Homes) and Bloomfield's own Union Park page were opened and state it.

land_banking.counterparty: Public improvement districts and municipal management districts (nine named on Bloomfield community pages)
land_banking.description: Bloomfield builds in communities where roads, utilities and amenities are financed through district assessments paid by the homeowner rather than through the lot price. Its own community pages name: Sonoma Public Improvement District (Sonoma Verde, Rockwall), Kaufman PID No. 1 (Georgetown at Kings Fort, Kaufman), Heritage PID No. 1 (Grand Heritage / Bear Creek, Lavon), Red Oak PID No. 1 (The Oaks, Red Oak), Anderson Crossing PID No. 1 (Trenton), North Grove PID (Waxahachie), Danieldale Homestead PID (Homestead at Daniel Farms and Creeks of Homestead, DeSoto), Joshua Farms Municipal Management District No. 1 (Silo Mills, Joshua, an 840-acre master plan) and Highway 380 Municipal Management District No. 1 (Union Park, Little Elm).
land_banking.source_title: Bloomfield Homes community pages, Tax / PID blocks (retrieved 2026-11-19); first of the pages read
land_banking.note: Based on 62 of the 137 community and section pages in Bloomfield's sitemap (the site began rate-limiting, so the crawl was stopped): the nine districts above are a floor, not a full list. No page read carried a separate MUD line. Bloomfield's own buyer guide (updated November 12, 2026) lists 15 communities with neither a MUD nor a PID and explains that developers use the districts to fund infrastructure up front (https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/blog/pid-mud-taxes-north-texas/). The pages do not say whether Bloomfield or a third party is the developer and landowner behind each district, and no bond offering document was read, so Bloomfield's role (district sponsor versus lot buyer) is not confirmed. Other pages read: https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/kaufman/georgetown-at-kings-fort-50s/ , https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/lavon/bear-creek-classic-50/ , https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/red-oak/the-oaks/ , https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/trenton/anderson-crossing/ , https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/waxahachie/the-oasis-at-north-grove-60/ , https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/desoto/creeks-of-homestead/ , https://www.bloomfieldhomes.com/new-homes/tx/joshua/silo-mills-classic-50/ .

debt.instrument: PARENT LEVEL (Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd., not a Bloomfield obligation): Tri Pointe acquisition bridge loan, up to JPY 835.1 billion
debt.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Conclusion of a Loan Agreement with Financial Covenants (2026-05-07)
debt.note: Signed May 7, 2026, disbursement planned May 11, bullet repayment planned May 10, 2027, no collateral. JPY 835.1 billion is the maximum and includes money for an assumed refinancing of Tri Pointe's own debt; the share price was about JPY 630 billion. Covenants: consolidated and parent-only net assets must each stay at or above 75% of the prior fiscal year-end level, and the R&I issuer rating must stay at BBB- or higher. By the November 5, 2026 results briefing the parent had raised JPY 350.0 billion of subordinated bonds and loans toward permanent financing and said the remaining JPY 260.0 billion would follow (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_3q_forecast_02_en.pdf); the exact bridge balance today is not stated. About $5.3B at JPY 158.53 per dollar (our conversion).

capital_events.description: Parent level: Sumitomo Forestry agreed to buy Tri Pointe Homes for $47.00 a share and laid out the funding plan: a bridge loan first, then permanent financing within about a year through bank borrowings, bonds and hybrid instruments, with no dilution of common equity. It also amended its articles so that bond-type class shares could be issued as one option (analysts at the briefing put the possible size at up to JPY 100 billion).
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Acquisition of Shares (Subsidiarization) of Tri Pointe Homes, Inc., presentation with script (2026-02-13)
capital_events.note: Bond-type class share detail from the February 20, 2026 Q&A (https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20260220_Q%26A_from_the_Briefing_on_the_Acquisition_of_Shares.pdf). The same Q&A says that in past US builder acquisitions the founders stayed on with 'a certain equity stake' while Sumitomo took a majority, and that the group is building a management structure for the point when founders eventually exit: the description fits Bloomfield, though Bloomfield is not named in that answer.

capital_events.description: Parent level: one-year bridge loan of up to JPY 835.1 billion signed with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation to fund the Tri Pointe purchase, repayable in one payment on May 10, 2027.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Conclusion of a Loan Agreement with Financial Covenants (2026-05-07)
capital_events.note: About $5.3B at JPY 158.53 per dollar (our conversion). The closing notice of May 14, 2026 put the price for the shares at about $4,003M (https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20260514_Notice_of_Completion_of_TriPointe_Homes_Acquisition.pdf).

capital_events.description: Parent level: R&I issuer rating shown as A+ (Stable) and short-term rating a-1, announced May 15, 2026, the day after the Tri Pointe closing. JCR issuer rating shown as AA- (Stable), announced June 18, 2026.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Credit Ratings and Corporate Bonds information (page as of September 2026)
capital_events.note: The page gives the current rating and announcement date only; whether either was an affirmation or a change was not checked at the agencies. On November 5, 2026 management said a downgrade is possible if the current business environment continues (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_3q_qanda_en.pdf).

capital_events.description: Parent level: full-year FY12/2026 forecast cut (recurring income from JPY 160.0 billion to JPY 115.0 billion, net income from JPY 95.0 billion to JPY 60.0 billion) on Tri Pointe goodwill, deal costs and interest, weaker US single-family income from buyer hesitation and incentives, and losses in US real estate.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding Revisions to the Financial Results Forecast (2026-08-07)
capital_events.note: At the August 10, 2026 Q&A management said DRB's margin had fallen while 'the other builders', which include Bloomfield, were still earning recurring income margins in the high teens, and that Dallas and Austin were showing signs of improvement (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_2q_qanda_en.pdf). Bloomfield is not named individually.

capital_events.note: About $1.54B at JPY 158.53 per dollar (our conversion).

capital_events.description: Parent level, third-quarter results: interest-bearing debt JPY 1,659.7 billion (JPY 769.5 billion at December 31, 2025), net interest-bearing debt JPY 1,448.5 billion, equity ratio 29.2% (39.0% a year-end earlier), net debt to equity about 1.4 times. JPY 350.0 billion of the Tri Pointe funding has been made permanent and JPY 260.0 billion remains. Management expects about JPY 10 billion of valuation losses on US real estate for sale in the fourth quarter and plans to raise cash by selling strategic shareholdings and being more selective in investments.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry FY12/2026 Third Quarter Financial Results and Full Year Forecast, presentation with transcript (2026-11-05)
capital_events.note: Valuation-loss and downgrade remarks from the November 5, 2026 analyst Q&A (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_3q_qanda_en.pdf). Interest-bearing debt is about $10.5B and net interest-bearing debt about $9.1B at JPY 158.53 per dollar (our conversion). For the five pre-Tri Pointe US builders, nine-month net sales fell 6.5% and recurring income fell 40.8% year on year, to a 9.1% margin (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_3q_fact_en.pdf).

joint_ventures.partner: P. Ryan Properties, Inc. (Donald and Deborah Dykstra) and TKJT, Inc. (Timothy and Karen Stewart)
joint_ventures.description: Bloomfield Homes, L.P. is itself a partnership between Sumitomo Forestry America and the founders' holding companies. Before the May 2017 step-up the partners were Sumitomo Forestry America 49.95%, P. Ryan Properties 44.95%, TKJT 5.0% and the general partner Bloomfield Properties, Inc. 0.1% (itself 50% owned by Sumitomo Forestry America). Sumitomo then bought a further 15%, mainly from P. Ryan Properties, to reach 65% including its indirect interest through the general partner, leaving the founders' side with 35%.
joint_ventures.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice regarding acquisition of additional equity interest in Bloomfield Homes, L.P. which will become a subsidiary (2017-04-28)
joint_ventures.note: Tagged Inferred because the ownership split comes from a 2017 notice and no newer percentage is published; the 35% founder share and its split between the two founders after 2017 are our arithmetic, not a stated figure. Still consistent with 2026 state records: both founders and Sumitomo Forestry designees sit on the boards of the L.P. and its general partner (https://comptroller.texas.gov/data-search/franchise-tax/32035542730 and https://comptroller.texas.gov/data-search/franchise-tax/32015762365), and TKJT, Inc. lists Timothy M. Stewart as president (https://comptroller.texas.gov/data-search/franchise-tax/32051121963, report year 2024). P. Ryan Properties' ownership by the Dykstras is as stated in the 2017 notice.

ma.counterparty: Tri Pointe Homes, Inc. (bought by Bloomfield's parent, Sumitomo Forestry; Bloomfield was not a party)
ma.description: Sumitomo Forestry completed its all-cash purchase of 100% of Tri Pointe Homes on May 14, 2026 (announced February 13, 2026; $47.00 a share; about $4,003M for the shares), funded by a JPY 835.1 billion SMBC bridge loan. Tri Pointe's markets include Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin and Houston.
ma.map_impact: Bloomfield's ownership and leadership did not change, but its parent group did: Bloomfield (rank 41) is now a sister of Tri Pointe (rank 19) and DRB Group, and the parent's Texas region has three group builders (DRB, Bloomfield, Tri Pointe), with Tri Pointe building in Bloomfield's only market and beside it in at least one master plan (Union Park). The group now reports 106,415 US lots and wants more of them under option; the parent's net debt to equity went from 0.5 to about 1.4 times, which bears on how much owned land it will fund at subsidiaries such as Bloomfield.
ma.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Completion of the Acquisition of Shares (Subsidiarization) of Tri Pointe Homes, Inc. (2026-05-14)
ma.note: Tri Pointe market list (Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin, Houston) from the February 13, 2026 acquisition presentation (https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20260213_Acquisition_of_Shares_Script.pdf); the three-builder Texas footprint from the Q3 FY12/2026 factbook business-area table (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_3q_fact_en.pdf); Union Park builder list from https://www.unionparkbyhillwood.com/builders. Role is recorded as Acquirer because the buyer is Bloomfield's parent.

gaps: Bloomfield lot count (owned, optioned, years of supply): not publicly disclosed. The parent reports only a combined figure for its five pre-Tri Pointe US builders.

Bloomfield debt, credit facility (size, maturity, agent bank), cash and liquidity: not publicly disclosed (private partnership consolidated into a Japanese parent; no SEC filings, no rated debt). Last stand-alone figures found are for FY2016 in the 2017 notice: turnover $321M, net profit $56M, total assets $235M, net assets $102M.

Lenders: not confirmed. A county-records aggregator (elementix.com/companies/bloomfield-homes) names Truist Bank, Third Coast Bank and Wells Fargo as top lenders of record, but the same page attributes Antares Acquisition, LLC to Bloomfield, and the Texas Comptroller record shows that entity is run from Irvine, CA by another builder's officers; its lender and model-home-investor lists are therefore not usable and are not recorded as facts.

Land-banking or lot-option financing partner for Bloomfield: none found in any source read. No public link between Bloomfield and Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis, TPG Angelo Gordon, DW Partners, Essential Housing, IHP Capital, Brookfield, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton or Forestar was found; the shared web-search allowance was exhausted before this run, so this rests on the parent's disclosures, Bloomfield's site and an EDGAR full-text search, not on a press search.

Whether Bloomfield is the developer and landowner behind the public improvement districts and the Joshua Farms municipal management district on its communities, and any bond amounts: not confirmed (no offering document read). The district list covers 62 of 137 community pages.

Current ownership split: the 65% Sumitomo Forestry stake is from the 2017 notice; no later percentage is published in English. Whether the founders hold put or call rights on their remaining interest is not disclosed.

Terms of parent funding to Bloomfield (intercompany loans, guarantees, dividends): not publicly disclosed. Intra-group loans and guarantees are eliminated in the parent's consolidated statements, so they do not show there.
M&A involving Bloomfield itself in 2025 or 2026 (as acquirer, target or change of ownership): none found in the parent's 2025 and 2026 news indexes, which were read in full.
Bloomfield's share of the parent's Texas unit sales and its own 2026 closings: not disclosed by the parent.

Moved out of M&A on verification (2026-11-19), because it is an internal reorganisation and not a transaction: Sumitomo Forestry consolidated sister company Brightland Homes (the former Gehan Homes) under DRB Group in March 2025, per the parent's February 13, 2026 Tri Pointe deal presentation (https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20260213_Acquisition_of_Shares_Script.pdf). Bloomfield was not a party; it remains a separately run, founder-led subsidiary.
